main.summary: Tao Hongjing replies to a letter from Secretary Xie with a brief praise of mountain and river scenery: high peaks, clear streams, rock walls, forests and bamboo, and the sights of morning and evening. He calls it an immortals' capital in the human world, and sighs that since Xie Lingyun no one has been able to share its wonder.
main.translation: The beauty of mountains and rivers has been talked about by all since ancient times. High peaks enter the clouds; clear streams show their bed. On the two banks the rock walls shine in five colours, giving each other light. Green woods and emerald bamboo are there in all four seasons. When the morning mist is about to clear, gibbons and birds cry out together; when the evening sun is about to sink, fish in the depths vie to leap. It is truly an immortals' capital within the realm of desire. Since Kangle, there has been no one else able to share in its wonder.

keyLines.en: The beauty of mountains and rivers has been talked about by all since ancient times.
keyLines.note: It goes straight to the point: the beauty of landscape is something that people of every age have shared in talking about.

keyLines.en: High peaks enter the clouds; clear streams show their bed.
keyLines.note: Two four-character parallel lines show how high the mountains are and how clear the water, with a spare touch.

keyLines.en: Green woods and emerald bamboo are there in all four seasons.
keyLines.note: It describes the forest and bamboo as evergreen and lovely in every season.

keyLines.line: 曉霧將歇，猿鳥亂鳴；夕日欲頹，沉鱗競躍
keyLines.en: When the morning mist is about to clear, gibbons and birds cry out together; when the evening sun is about to sink, fish in the depths vie to leap.
keyLines.note: Two times of day, morning and evening, show the sounds and colours of living creatures, with stillness and movement setting each other off.

keyLines.en: It is truly an immortals' capital within the realm of desire.
keyLines.note: The verdict of the whole piece: this is a rare fairyland in the human world.

keyLines.line: 自康樂以來，未復有能與其奇者
keyLines.en: Since Kangle, there has been no one else able to share in its wonder.
keyLines.note: Through Xie Lingyun (Duke of Kangle), it says that only someone who loves landscape deeply can feel such beauty, with a hint of self-praise.

glossary.en: zhong shu - Secretary of the Secretariat
glossary.note: An official title, a member of the Secretariat. 'Xie zhong shu' means a friend named Xie who held that post.

glossary.en: wu se jiao hui - five colours shining on each other
glossary.note: The rock walls show many colours that light each other up.
Fish that lie deep in the water.

glossary.en: yu jie - the realm of desire
glossary.note: A Buddhist term for the world of beings with desires. Here it means the human world.
Xie Lingyun, who inherited the title Duke of Kangle and was famous for his landscape poems.

main.background: Tao Hongjing was a Daoist scholar of the Southern dynasties, in the Qi and Liang periods (479-557). He lived in retirement on Mount Mao and was called the 'prime minister in the mountains'. This is a short letter in reply to a friend, and in a few dozen characters it paints a landscape; it is a famous small piece of landscape writing from the Six Dynasties.
